relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a biopsy-diagnosed Danon disease patient ("A diagnosis of Danon disease was confirmed by biopsy results."), with a previously reported patient [7] and the patient's affected mother; no LAMP2 variant is printed or reported for anyone.
method_note: Read the paper by hand; built the JSON with a short script in scratch and checked every span verbatim. No genetic testing and no LAMP2 variant is reported for any person (diagnosis by biopsy/electron microscopy and LAMP-2 protein deficiency on immunofluorescence), so the variants table is empty; n_patients_reported left null because the authors state no number of patients with a LAMP2 variant. In scope: the case patient ('patient'); the mother (described in relation to the patient, died suddenly at 44 with dilated cardiomyopathy and pacemaker; not tested); the previously reported 24-year-old male of ref [7] (Figure 7 legend and Discussion; individual-level facts given). The sister mentioned only as next of kin for consent gets no row (no clinical or testing information). The 1981 'two boys' of ref [1] and the general literature statements get no rows (no individual-level facts). cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null: the paper does not say the case patient was described before; ref [7] (same authors, SCMR case of the week) is a different, previously reported patient. Creatine kinase 510 u/L is printed inside the parenthesis of 'elevated liver enzymes (...)', so it was recorded as observed elevated CK; the paper does not state a reference range. Both-ventricle hypertrophy recorded as LVH and RVH. Mother's 'dilated cardiomyopathy' recorded as observed for the dilated-LV checklist item. For ref [7], 'hypertrophic cardiomyopathy' is taken from the Discussion sentence citing [7]; the LVH checklist item was left not reported because ventricular hypertrophy is not stated directly; 'preserved EF' recorded as excluded reduced ejection fraction, but the dilated-or-hypokinetic checklist item left not reported because 'mild contractile dysfunction' is also stated. Patient's age 19 is the age at admission; he died two weeks later (age at death not stated, left null). No stacked cells; no tables. No contradictions found.
